raw_chunks.raw_source: ## The last programming exercise

raw_chunks.content: The final programming exercise on this course is creating a small game of your own with pygame. The exercise template contains some images for you to use. Please don't use any other images in your game, or others will not be able to test your game based on the source code alone.

raw_chunks.content: The subject of the game is up to you, but it should be about as complicated as the Sokoban example in this part of the material. The game should contain the following features:
raw_chunks.raw_source: The subject of the game is up to you, but it should be about as complicated as the Sokoban example in this part of the material. The game should contain the following features:

raw_chunks.content:
* The game has a sprite the player can move in some way
* The game has some collectable items and/or enemies 
* The player needs to be set a clear task in the game
* The game contains a counter which tells the player how they are doing in the game
* The source code for the game is divided into functions like in the Sokoban example

raw_chunks.raw_source: ## How part 14 is graded

raw_chunks.content: The goal of this part is to build a small, working game. As this part contains only a single task, *you get points for effort*. Please submit your game even if you can't get it to work quite the way you wanted to.

raw_chunks.raw_source: ## Some game ideas

raw_chunks.content: It is completely up to you what your game will be about, but here are some ideas to help you get started. Remember the material in part 13; those examples can help you work on your ideas, too.

raw_chunks.content: A collecting game
raw_chunks.raw_source: ### A collecting game

raw_chunks.content:
* The player moves the robot with the arrow keys.
* A coin appears in a random location on the screen. When the robot reaches it, the coin moves to a new location.
* There are also monsters on the screen, and the robot must avoid them.

* Coins rain from the sky. The robot must collect these.
* Also monsters rain from the sky. The robot must avoid these.

* How well is it programmed? Is the code readable, and does it make appropriate use of classes and functions?
